_note: B0 harness cross-check. Published MIRAGE accuracies, as fractions. No-RAG rows are the 'None' (no-retrieval) baseline; BM25 rows are MedRAG with the BM25 retriever over the Textbooks corpus, chosen because that is the corpus our BM25 arm runs over (MedRAG/textbooks). Reported with +/- CIs in the paper; point estimates only here.
_source: Xiong, Jin, Lu, Zhang (2024), 'Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medicine', Findings of ACL 2024, arXiv:2402.13178v2. No-RAG = Table 7 'None' row; BM25 = Table 7 BM25/Textbooks row. Cross-checked against the Table 6 GPT-3.5 CoT row (identical).
_applicability: These numbers are GPT-3.5. The paper reports no per-dataset BM25 breakdown for any other backbone, and does not cover Llama-3.1-8B at all. An absolute comparison against a different backbone is not a harness check -- see _delta_note. Nearest open-weight anchor for the No-RAG side only is Llama2-70B (Table 6 CoT): MMLU-Med 0.5739, MedQA-US 0.4784, MedMCQA 0.4260, PubMedQA 0.4220, BioASQ-YN 0.6117.
_delta_note: The backbone-robust check is the SIGN of (BM25 - No-RAG), not the absolute level. Published on MedQA-US: +0.0150 (BM25 helps). A run where that delta is negative has a retrieval problem regardless of backbone. Use delta_crosscheck() for this.
_pubmedqa_caveat: PubMedQA* in the source table is the reduced setting the paper marks with an asterisk, not the full PubMedQA test set.
